result_json.message:
feat(plan-217 phase 1): operator-authorized mechanical checklist repair (W1)

Add 5x plan repair-checklists (--plan draft / --run source or execution,
--dry-run/--apply) with a pure prefix-only proof module, a versioned
plan-checklist-repair lineage kind folded like a text amendment (no new
revision, no evidence invalidation), source-repair carry-over at bind
that keeps the original approval commit, repair hints on drift and
zero-item checklist failures, and unit/integration coverage.

result_json.notes:
Phase 1 (W1) is done and committed as 7039ed14. Only the Phase 1 boxes are checked; Phases 2–5 are untouched. In the plan file, the only change is those six checkbox toggles.

Checks run: bun run lint and bun run typecheck are clean. bun run test passed with 4266 tests and no failures. The focused asset suite (upgrade.test.ts plus implementation-review-governance.test.ts) passed 48/48.

What was built:
- **Repair logic and proof (src/plan-schema/checklist-repair.ts):** finds the completion-gate lists in each phase and adds unchecked boxes to their plain top-level items. The proof allows only those list-prefix changes and toggles of boxes that already existed. It refuses fenced examples and anything outside the contract or outside a phase. When a candidate adds a box already ticked, the preview shows it reset to unchecked. Lists it can't place unambiguously need an explicit `--phase`/`--lines` choice. Phases with no list, or only indented sub-items, are reported as author work. The parser now exports `phaseSectionRanges`, so the repair and the item counts use the same phase boundaries.
- **New record kind `plan-checklist-repair`:** has a strict decoder, a paired budget line and step, and keys that make retries idempotent. Reading the run's history treats it like a text amendment. It moves only the authorized plan anchor and rechecks the proof on replay. It does not create a new revision, and existing evidence, findings and phase completions stay valid. It is wired into the store, lineage replay and the amendment lineage tail.
- **Binding from a repaired source:** the source's repairs are re-checked and copied onto the execution run in the same atomic append as the binding, each copy recording its origin. The binding keeps the original `approvedPlanCommit`, source, policy and ledger. A repair attempted on a source that already has a binding is refused and points to the execution run instead.
- **Command `5x plan repair-checklists`:** `--plan` (draft) or `--run`, with `--dry-run` or `--apply`. Apply on a run requires `--reason`. Optional `--phase`, `--lines`, `--intent` and `--no-checkpoint`.
  - The `--plan` form defers to the governing run's `--run` command when the plan is already approved or bound.
  - The `--run` form commits only the plan file, then re-proves the bytes git actually holds in case a hook changed them.
  - An interrupted apply resumes against the existing repair commit, and an identical retry returns the stored receipt.
  - A changed candidate under `--intent` is shown again as a fresh preview; an unchanged one is applied. A concurrent journal write fails cleanly with nothing recorded.
- **Recovery hints:** drift errors at admission and at bind now include the repair command, in the message and in `detail.repairCommand`. A phase with zero checklist items now explains how to repair it; the error code is still `PHASE_CHECKLIST_INCOMPLETE`.

Tests added:
- `test/unit/plan-schema/checklist-repair.test.ts`
- `test/unit/commands/plan-checklist-repair.test.ts`
- new lineage tests in `implementation-amendment.test.ts`, including evidence preservation and a later semantic amendment
- `test/integration/commands/plan-repair-checklists.test.ts`, covering the draft form, a source repair followed by bind, and an execution run blocked by drift. That run is repaired with no reviewer steps, its new boxes are checked and the phase is completed on the same run, then the index is rebuilt.

Choices the plan left open:
- Indented sub-bullets stay plain, as part of their parent item. A manual edit that adds boxes to them still passes the proof.
- Recording a schema migration on a source that already has a checklist repair is refused.
- Text-amendment guards created before a repair go stale, the same as after any other lineage change.

Workflow assets: no prompts, skills or skeletons were changed. That work belongs to Phase 5 (W5) under the plan's asset matrix; Phase 1 only adds the CLI command and runtime messages.

feat(plan-217 phase 2): shared executability diagnostics with repair-first boundaries (W2)

Add a pure diagnosePlanExecutability result over the authoritative phase
parse (no phases, duplicate ids, zero-item phases incl. COMPLETE headings,
nonblocking mixed gate-list warnings) with locations and deterministic
repair availability. The parser, phase ranges and repair module now share
one fence/comment filter so counts and validation agree.

plan phases reports additive per-phase executable flags and executability
diagnostics/next commands without failing; help examples use the real
.data.phases[] fields. Plan review render/invoke/record returns
PLAN_REPAIR_REQUIRED (author_revision, ready-to-run --plan preview) in every
budget mode before any reviewer, baseline or gate. Author delegation
returns PLAN_CHECKLIST_REPAIR_REQUIRED with the exact --run/--plan repair
for a mechanically repairable target phase and preserves the run; author-
only gaps warn. Phase completion and plan-run completion reuse the same
result (completion stays nonblocking).

Tests cover the incident fixture, COMPLETE headings, nested-only items,
explanatory bullets, prose gates, supported markers, fences/comments/notes,
schema 0/1 authority, the compact issue plan, and recovery paths in
enforced/advisory/off/non-budgeted and approved-run flows. Phase-less test
fixtures gain one executable phase; the Phase 1 integration fixture now
simulates a legacy pre-gate approval.

result_json.notes:
Phase 2 (W2) is implemented. All 6 checklist items are checked; that is the only edit to the plan. Lint and typecheck are clean. The full suite passed 4301/0. A later lint fix to two test files was re-run on its own: 9/9 pass. The focused asset and issue-resolution suites also pass (258/0).

- **Shared diagnostics:** new `diagnosePlanExecutability` in `src/plan-schema/checklist-repair.ts`. It reports plans with no phases, duplicate phase ids, and phases with no items, including a zero-item phase whose heading says COMPLETE. Each report has its line and says which fix applies: automatic (mechanical), pick the right list with `--phase`/`--lines`, or author work. A gate list that mixes checkbox and plain items only produces a warning.
- **Parser alignment:** `parsePlan`, `phaseSectionRanges` and the repair module now share one `literalPlanLines` rule. Lines inside code fences or HTML comment blocks no longer count as phases or items, so the parser and the diagnostics give the same counts.
- **`plan phases`:** adds an `executable` flag per phase and an `executability` block with diagnostics and the repair commands to run, filled in for the run that governs the plan when there is one. It never fails because a phase has zero items. The help examples now use the real `.data.phases[]` fields.
- **Plan review:** template render, invoke and record return `PLAN_REPAIR_REQUIRED` (route `author_revision`, `next` = the `--plan` repair preview) in enforced, advisory, off and plans with no Delivery Budget. It fires after the existing budget check and before any baseline capture, reviewer run or gate.
- **Author delegation (render/invoke):** if the target phase has no items and an automatic or line-selected fix exists, it returns `PLAN_CHECKLIST_REPAIR_REQUIRED` with the exact `--run` (bound run) or `--plan` command and leaves the run active. If only author work can fix it, it warns instead of blocking.
- **Completion:** the phase-completion check uses the same result to name the repair. Completing a plan-review run adds a `plan_executability` field to the output but never blocks; the fix is the `--run <source>` form before binding.

Decisions you may want to check:
1. Author-only gaps on approved plans warn rather than block. Completion already refuses those phases, and a new block with no repair path would be another dead end.
2. Several plan-review test fixtures had no phases (or used a bare `## Phase 1` heading, which the parser has never counted). I added one executable phase to each. I did not widen the parser.
3. The Phase 1 integration fixture can no longer record a fresh approval of a malformed plan, because the new recording check refuses it. It now simulates a legacy approval: the verdict is recorded against a fixed working copy while the committed, sealed plan keeps the malformed bytes. All Phase 1 behaviour tests still pass.

New tests are in `test/unit/plan-schema/executability.test.ts`, `test/integration/commands/plan-executability.test.ts`, and a new approved-run test in `plan-repair-checklists.test.ts` that covers block, repair and resume on the same run.

result_json.notes:
Fixed the admitted Phase 2 findings R1-R4 and nothing else. There are no edits to the governing plan; all Phase 2 checkboxes were already checked.

R1: The native (template.handler) and invoke author delegation checks now pass the recorded schema of a bound execution (expectedSchemaForStore). An ungoverned file still infers its schema from its markers. New caller-level tests use a schema-0 binding over a plan with schema-1-looking markers. Both tests fail without the fix (PLAN_CHECKLIST_REPAIR_REQUIRED) and pass with it.

R2: The shared literalPlanLines filter now handles two more cases:
- A backtick line only opens a fence when its info string has no backticks, so a triple-backtick inline span no longer hides items. Tilde fences may still have backticks.
- A multiline HTML comment opened after prose now hides the lines that follow until it closes.
- A `<!--` inside inline code opens nothing.
New tests cover parsing, diagnostics and repair eligibility in both directions. They fail against the old parser.

R3: The invoke reviewer-plan(-continued) executability preflight now runs outside the run-guarded block, for any resolved plan, before a provider or session is created. This matches native rendering. In invoke, params.run is always filled in (explicitly or from the ambient run) before this point, so the old path could not actually be bypassed. The test pins the case with no --run and a nonbudgeted (mode off) context: zero provider creations and sessions on refusal, then success after the repair. It would also pass on the old code.

R4: evaluatePhaseChecklist, used by protocol validate and phase finish, now refuses zero executable items even when the heading says COMPLETE. It returns the mechanical repair command when one exists and author guidance otherwise. Inspection still shows the COMPLETE display flag. New tests in protocol-validate and phase-finish fail without the fix.

Verification: lint clean, typecheck clean, full suite 4310 pass / 0 fail.
